investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new agent pods. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by resource type and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"; the other 4 are excluded by node affinity/selector mismatch. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 136–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive or nodes were re-labeled, effective capacity is reduced even if total cluster size appears adequate.

Tertiary — missing or under-provisioned kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool: the cluster may not have been scaled to meet concurrent remote-agent demand, or a node group autoscaler has not yet added capacity.
Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots at the time of the eval run, which could resolve without intervention if workloads complete.

Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were produced, causing a complete contract gap against the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.

The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With no preemption victims available and no schedulable node, every eval pod that attempts to create a remote agent is stuck Unschedulable for ~136–151 seconds before the eval runner times out and records a failure. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion event localized to the kata peer-pod VM pool, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the state of the cluster at the time of the run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new agent pods. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by resource type and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"; the other 4 are excluded by node affinity/selector mismatch. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 136–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive or nodes were re-labeled, effective capacity is reduced even if total cluster size appears adequate.

Tertiary — missing or under-provisioned kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool: the cluster may not have been scaled to meet concurrent remote-agent demand, or a node group autoscaler has not yet added capacity.
Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots at the time of the eval run, which could resolve without intervention if workloads complete.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are Ready and advertising non-zero allocatable slots, catching node pool shrinkage or misconfiguration independently of agent creation.
Introduce a time-series eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization over successive runs to detect gradual capacity creep before full exhaustion occurs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were produced, causing a complete contract gap against the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With no preemption victims available and no schedulable node, every eval pod that attempts to create a remote agent is stuck Unschedulable for ~136–151 seconds before the eval runner times out and records a failure. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion event localized to the kata peer-pod VM pool, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the state of the cluster at the time of the run.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion on the only 2 eligible nodes.

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck for 136s, latencyMs=140638 — confirms the same resource constraint blocked agent creation.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 146s, latencyMs=151491 — confirms the constraint persisted across sequential eval runs spanning ~5 minutes.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150389, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-01T19:10:37.134Z — the eval ran to near-timeout before failing, consistent with a pod stuck in Pending until the eval runner gave up.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were collected, confirming the agent pod never reached a running state where the runtime could respond.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — the contract gap is total, consistent with the probe never reaching the agent runtime.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — if the pod is never scheduled, createAgent cannot return and no evidence is emitted.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared kata VM pool is the common dependency.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 peer-pod-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agent pods or leaked/zombie pods that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the label or taint required by the remote-agent pod spec, meaning the effective schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

[Possible] Leaked or stuck agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being released: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete a prior agent pod, its VM slot would remain allocated and reduce available capacity for subsequent runs.

[Possible] Cluster-level quota or limit on kata.peerpods.io/vm that is set too low relative to concurrent eval demand: if multiple eval runs or other workloads compete for the same VM slots simultaneously, the pool can be transiently exhausted.

[Lower likelihood] A recent infrastructure change reduced the number of peer-pod-eligible nodes from more than 2 to exactly 2, shrinking the schedulable pool below the minimum needed to absorb eval traffic.

reproductionSteps.details: Run kubectl describe node against each of the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector and look at the Allocatable and Allocated Resources sections for kata.peerpods.io/vm.

reproductionSteps.details: Query the cluster for pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests that are in Running or Pending state to determine whether prior eval cleanup failed.

reproductionSteps.details: Run kubectl get nodes --show-labels and compare against the node affinity/selector in the remote-agent pod spec to confirm the 4/2 split is expected or a misconfiguration.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm Kubernetes resource pool
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names this extended resource as exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, directly blocking all remote-agent pod scheduling.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same Unschedulable root cause, indicating the entire remote-agent provisioning path is blocked at the infrastructure layer.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The createAgent call at line 1918 depends on a schedulable kata peer-pod VM; when none is available the probe cannot produce any evidence and the contract gap is total.

affectedAreas.label: Remote-agent pod node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, permanently limiting the schedulable pool to 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion on those nodes.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata-peer-pod-eligible nodes immediately for kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization to determine whether the pool is currently exhausted or was transiently exhausted at eval run time.

Audit all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests in the cluster to identify any leaked or zombie pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs.

If VM slots are confirmed exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes needs to be increased, or whether additional nodes need to be labeled to match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector.

Investigate why 4 of 6 cluster nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector — confirm this is intentional architecture and not label drift that has reduced the schedulable pool below its intended size.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent eval runner that queries node capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm before attempting pod creation, so the eval can emit a more actionable SKIP or WARN status with capacity details rather than timing out after 136–151 seconds.

Review the withCleanup mechanism in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure agent pods and their VM slots are reliably released even when the eval probe fails mid-execution, to prevent slot leakage across runs.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is persistent or was transient at the time of the original run. A pass on re-run suggests transient slot exhaustion; a repeat fail confirms ongoing capacity shortage.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether VM slots are exhausted and how many are currently consumed vs. available.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether zombie or leaked eval pods are holding VM slots that should have been released by the withCleanup wrapper.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Verify node affinity/selector label coverage across all 6 nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4/2 node split is intentional or whether nodes have lost required labels, shrinking the eligible pool unexpectedly.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that all three checks share the same infrastructure bottleneck and that no check can pass independently while the VM pool is exhausted.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (not fully allocated), the exhaustion hypothesis is wrong and the cause lies elsewhere (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or runtime error before scheduling).

If a fresh eval run immediately after this failure succeeds without any cluster changes, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior eval's pods were released between runs) rather than a persistent capacity problem.

If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as an extended resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause such as a node label mismatch or taint toleration gap.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed at the same time with a similar message, the failure scope would be broader than the kata peer-pod pool and would implicate a shared upstream dependency.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes, the resource exhaustion message may reflect a misconfigured node capacity advertisement rather than actual slot consumption.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all eligible nodes and fails with a warning before slot exhaustion reaches 100%, providing earlier signal than a scheduling timeout.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) and alerts if any are found in a non-terminal state, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust the pool.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3), alerting if label drift reduces the eligible pool.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to emit a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulingLatencyMs, schedulerMessage) even on failure, so future investigations can distinguish scheduling failures from application-layer failures without relying solely on the free-text check message.
